maria-ml: Quick sync — we need to size a Dedicated pool for the new 30B quantized model (int8-ish) across us-west-2 + eu-west-1. Target SLO p95 <= 120ms for max prompt 256 tokens, baseline steady traffic ~200 req/s (99% US). Looking for GPU mix + concurrency headroom. any quick calc or past run numbers?
jonah: For that SLO and 256 tok, H100s looked best in benchmarks for latencies. But costy. How much burst traffic expected?
maria-ml: Burst factor ~2x for short windows (5-10m). We want autoscaler headroom to avoid cold fallbacks. Prefer to prioritize US capacity.
amy_v: L40s gave decent throughput for 30B quant in our 8-bit runs, p95 ~150ms at concurrency 8/gpu. H100 at concurrency 12/gpu hit p95 ~95ms. Numbers depend on kernel and kv cache warm state.
rafael: Key thing: kernel selection and continuous batching affect p95 a lot. Our perf runs used custom fused attention kernel + kv cache pinned. If you use default kernels, expect +20-30ms. Also check memory for extra cache when context grows.
infra-bot: perf-run: model=redwood-30b-quant, region=us-west-2, hw=H100-80GB, batch=1..16, concurrency=12, p50=28ms, p95=98ms, throughput=18 req/s per GPU (sustained)
infra-bot: perf-run: model=redwood-30b-quant, region=us-west-2, hw=L40S-48GB, concurrency=8, p50=38ms, p95=152ms, throughput=12 req/s per GPU
jonah: If we need 200 rps steady and 2x burst, target capacity peak=400 rps. With H100 @18 rps/GPU -> ~23 GPUs peak. Add 25% autoscale headroom => ~29 GPUs. For L40S @12 rps/GPU -> ~34 peak, +25% => ~43 GPUs.
maria-ml: That matches my quick calc. Can you paste the calc snippet?
jonah: Sure — sample: ```
// quick capacity calc
steady_rps = 200
burst_factor = 2.0
peak_rps = steady_rps * burst_factor
rps_per_gpu_h100 = 18
gpus_needed_peak = ceil(peak_rps / rps_per_gpu_h100)
autoscale_buffer = 0.25
gpus_provision = ceil(gpus_needed_peak * (1 + autoscale_buffer))
```
amy_v: Also model variants: consider offering a quant-4bit variant for cheaper path. In production we can route lower-priority traffic to quant4 (p95 ~140ms on L40S) and keep priority traffic on H100 quant8. Saves $$ on reserved capacity.
rafael: Kernel fallback plan: if H100 custom kernel fails, fallback to vendor kernel which increases p95 by ~30ms. Need rollout policy in console to fallback to a compatible variant with graceful throttling.
ops-sre: For autoscaler params, suggest min=8 (us-west), max=48, scale_step=4, cooldown=120s for target tracking based on sustained cpu/gpu util and request queue depth. Also set burst reserve = 15% spot of max to handle sudden spikes.
jonah: Example autoscale policy snippet: ```json
{
  "region":"us-west-2",
  "min_gpus":8,
  "max_gpus":48,
  "scale_step":4,
  "target_rps_per_gpu":14,
  "cooldown_s":120,
  "burst_reserve_pct":15
}
```
maria-ml: Nice. Any thoughts on cross-region split? We wanted 90% US, 10% EU. That means for H100 plan above, us-west needs ~26 GPUs reserved, eu-west ~3. Allow eu to be smaller but with faster cold start fallback route to hosted models.
amy_v: Yup — keep eu pool small and rely on fallback to hosted for large bursts to avoid over-reserving expensive GPUs in eu. Document that in runbook.
rafael: One more: quantization QA — we saw small regressions on instruction-following for 30B int8. Add eval suite (1000 prompts) to rollouts and fail if quality delta >1.5% BLEU/ROUGE or >5% for business-critical prompts.
ops-sre: Action items: 1) provision US H100 pool 29 GPUs reserved, autoscale max 48. 2) EU L40S pool 4 GPUs reserved, autoscale max 12. 3) Enable canary rollout with eval suite gating and kernel fallback. 4) Add cost dashboard.
maria-ml: I'll file a ticket with those numbers and ask finance for reserved commit estimate. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
jonah: I'll run a final perf sweep with the custom kernel and attach logs to the ticket.
rafael: I'll add the eval set and quality gating to the rollout config.
ops-sre: I'll draft autoscaler policy and runbook.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary started for redwood-30b-quant -> us-west-2 (3 GPU canary). status=running
maria-ml: Keep this thread updated with any perf diffs.
